To catch up users, many verification photos were collected from slimgur and other photo sites and reposted on a now banned subreddit. In light of this, I think it is important for users to be aware of protecting their privacy. Always be cautious of what you post online, don’t underestimate how one photo can bring you down (see:Anthony Weiner)

To protect your privacy I recommend the following items:

  1. Do not show your face – This is the easiest identifier you have and is not needed for verification, do not take the risk. It is easy to reverse image search to a Facebook account. Voat was removed from their webserver, imagine what fatties will do if they know who you are and where you live.

  2. Wear different clothes, hide identifying features and use a generic background (i.e. a white wall). A bedroom can be just as identifying as your face as everyone’s is unique.

  3. Remove EXIF data – Geographical and additional data is stored in photos. Paste into paint (remove your face!) and save the photo to remove the EXIF data. Slimgur and imgur remove the EXIF data upon upload.

  4. Make an account on a photo sharing site and set the photo to private. This removes the photo from the main browsing page.

/u/technician90 has given us moderator status on slimgur to remove verification photos after being verified, which is very helpful and appreciated. Even so, you should not neglect your privacy when posting a photo online. It may be copied before it is deleted or deletion could be overlooked.

Regarding verification

During verification I will message each user confirming verification prior to implementing the flair. It is easier to review all verification requests and add flairs simultaneously after emptying the mail box rather than sequentially. If you are the first message read your flair may take 20-30min to be added. If your flair does not appear after an hour please message the FLAIR account.

There have been a few users providing photos from a few months prior, we cannot accept these verification requests. It is very unlikely, however someone could have stolen the photo, made an account on voat with the same user name and try to get verified. Let the stolen verification photos be a testament to the possibilities. We must be bureaucratic and cautious with verification requests to avoid any improper verifications. I know it is a pain to take a new photo, but I hope you understand why we must reject these requests.

The last thing we want is for users to be harmed by posting here. All of FPH has been wrapped in controversy the last 10 days and emotions are high. Everything will settle in the coming weeks; during this time please be careful.
